Tianjin Binhai Commercial World Co., Ltd. v. Tianjin Tianyi Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. and Wang Xifeng — Dispute over Property Ownership

Ruling Summary

1. According to the provisions of Article 13, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the principle of good faith shall be followed in civil litigation. If a party, after filing a claim and after the people's court has rendered an effective judgment, denies the basic facts on which the claim was based and applies for retrial on this ground, such conduct violates the principle of good faith, and the people's court shall not support it.

2. The provisions of Article 15 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Sales Contracts for Commercial Housing regarding the time limit for exercising the right of rescission shall apply only to disputes over sales contracts for commercial housing as referred to in that Interpretation. For other contracts for the sale of houses, if the law has no provisions or the parties have no agreement on the time limit for exercising the right of rescission, the right shall be exercised within a reasonable time limit in accordance with the provisions of Article 95 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. What constitutes a "reasonable time limit" shall be determined by the people's court in light of the specific facts of the case.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2012) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 310

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Retrial Applicant): Tianjin Tianyi Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at the intersection of Jingu Road and Laodong Road, Gegu Town, Jinnan District, Tianjin.

Legal representative: Wang Qing, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Duan Zhiping, lawyer of Beijing Kangda Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Respondent): Tianjin Binhai Commercial World Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 94 Shanghai Road, Tanggu District, Tianjin.

Legal representative: Yang Fenglan, Chairwoman of the Company.

Respondent (Third Party at First Instance): Wang Xifeng (formerly known as Wang Xifeng), female, Han ethnicity, born on September 29, 1962, residing at Room 1501, Gate 5, Hongda Apartment, Tanggu District, Tianjin.

Retrial Applicant Tianjin Tianyi Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianyi Company), in the case of dispute over property ownership with Respondents Tianjin Binhai Commercial World Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Binhai Company) and Wang Xifeng, being dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2009) Jin Gao Min Zai Zi No. 0010 of the Tianjin High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Retrial Judgment), applied to this Court for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review the case, and the review has now been concluded.

Tianyi Company applied for retrial on the following grounds:

(1) The Retrial Judgment erred in finding that Binhai Company failed to properly perform its obligation of cooperation, which constitutes a factual error. According to Article 5 and Article 16 of the Measures for the Administration of Commercial Housing Mortgage Loans of the Agricultural Bank of China, a borrower must satisfy two important conditions: first, having already signed a commercial housing sales contract or agreement with the seller; and second, having already paid no less than 40% of the total price of the commercial housing purchased as a down payment. When applying for a loan from the bank, the borrower must provide the signed commercial housing sales contract and proof of down payment. The nominal buyer Wang Xifeng has not yet signed a formal housing sales contract with Binhai Company, the issue of the down payment has not been resolved, and Wang Xifeng has no evidence that the bank accepted her loan application. Therefore, the conditions for Wang Xifeng to obtain a mortgage loan were not fulfilled, Binhai Company's obligation to cooperate in obtaining the loan had not yet commenced, and it is impossible that Binhai Company failed to properly perform its obligation of cooperation.

(2) The Retrial Judgment erroneously applied the law. 1. Where Binhai Company did not breach the contract and Tianyi Company had already overdue payment, Binhai Company indeed had the right of rescission. However, in accordance with the provisions of Article 95 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and with reference to the provisions of Article 15, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Sales Contracts for Commercial Housing (hereinafter referred to as the Judicial Interpretation on Commercial Housing Sales Contracts), Binhai Company failed to exercise its right of rescission within a reasonable time limit (3 months) after being urged by Tianyi Company, and its right of rescission had been extinguished before the lawsuit was filed. Therefore, the Retrial Judgment's finding that Binhai Company had the right to rescind the contract erroneously applied the law. 2. Even if Binhai Company breached the contract, this case should not apply Article 94, Item (4) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, but instead Item (3) thereof, and Binhai Company had no right to directly sue for rescission of the contract without first issuing a demand. In fact, Binhai Company not only never demanded that Tianyi Company pay the remaining amount, but also never raised any objection to Tianyi Company's renewal of leases with the tenants of the subject property and its continued operation for as long as half a year. Tianyi Company had ample reason to believe that Binhai Company was willing to continue performing the contract and was willing to give Tianyi Company sufficient time to raise the remaining purchase price. 3. The Retrial Judgment's application of Article 167 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China concerning contracts for installment sales was erroneous. A contract for installment sale refers to a special sales contract in which the parties agree that after the subject matter is delivered to the buyer, the buyer shall pay the total price payable to the seller in installments within a certain period. The typical characteristic of a contract for installment sale is that after the subject matter is delivered, the price is paid in installments. In this case, before the delivery of the subject property, the down payment of RMB 34,000,000 had been fully paid; after delivery, the remaining purchase price of RMB 51,000,000 was to be paid in a lump sum by Tianyi Company through a bank loan, and there was no issue of installment payment. Therefore, the contract involved in this case is not a contract for installment sale and should not be subject to Article 167 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. 4. In balancing the interests of both parties, the Retrial Judgment did not genuinely consider the factor of the appreciation in value of the subject property, resulting in a judgment that overly favored Binhai Company and was manifestly unfair to Tianyi Company. First, due to the substantial appreciation of the subject property by hundreds of millions of yuan, the benefit obtained by Binhai Company from the rescission of the contract far exceeded the rental income it lost as a result of the rescission. Therefore, even if the contract were rescinded, Binhai Company would not sustain actual losses. Based on the principle that compensation for breach of contract should be limited to actual losses, where Binhai Company had no actual losses, the Retrial Judgment should not have ordered Tianyi Company to return rental income to Binhai Company as compensation for breach of contract. If the Retrial Judgment considered that upon rescission of the contract Tianyi Company should return to Binhai Company the rental income obtained from the use of the subject property, then on the basis of reciprocity, Binhai Company should also return to Tianyi Company the benefit obtained from the use of the down payment of RMB 34,000,000. The Retrial Judgment only ordered Binhai Company to return the interest on the down payment, which is manifestly unfair. Second, if the subject contract should be rescinded and this was caused solely by Tianyi Company's breach, then the appreciation in value of the subject property should of course belong entirely to Binhai Company. However, since the Retrial Judgment found that Tianyi Company, Wang Xifeng, and Binhai Company were all responsible for the failure to continue performance of the contract, the appreciation in value of the subject property cannot be enjoyed solely by Binhai Company; Tianyi Company should also be entitled to a certain interest. Tianyi Company applied for retrial pursuant to Article 179, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2007 (i.e., Article 200, Items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China).

This Court found upon review: Binhai Company filed an action with the Tianjin Second Intermediate People's Court on June 28, 2006, and the court accepted the case on July 18, 2006. The Retrial Judgment's finding that Binhai Company filed the action on July 18, 2006 is erroneous, and this Court hereby corrects it. This Court is of the opinion that the following issues are involved in the retrial review: (1) whether the ground for retrial asserted by Tianyi Company that the Retrial Judgment made factual errors can be established; and (2) whether the ground for retrial asserted by Tianyi Company that the Retrial Judgment erroneously applied the law can be established.

(1) Whether the ground for retrial asserted by Tianyi Company that the Retrial Judgment made factual errors can be established

The Retrial Judgment found that "Binhai Company did not properly perform its obligation of cooperation by providing the ownership certificate and the state-owned land use certificate for the subject property" and on that basis found that Tianyi Company, Wang Xifeng, and Binhai Company should each bear corresponding responsibility for the failure to continue performance of the contract. Tianyi Company applied for retrial, asserting that it was impossible for Binhai Company to have failed to properly perform its obligation of cooperation, and on this ground argued that the Retrial Judgment made factual errors.

Upon examination: Binhai Company filed a claim to rescind the subject agreements and for Tianyi Company to bear liability for breach of contract. Tianyi Company filed a counterclaim, alleging that Binhai Company failed to perform its obligation of cooperation as agreed, resulting in Tianyi Company's inability to obtain a loan and the non-payment of the balance, and requested the continued performance of the agreements and compensation by Binhai Company of liquidated damages of RMB 2,550,000 and corresponding bank interest of RMB 3,250,000. The first instance judgment found that it was reasonable for Binhai Company not to submit the original ownership certificate and state-owned land use certificate, and could not find that Binhai Company failed to cooperate or breached the contract. After the first instance judgment was rendered, Tianyi Company appealed on the grounds that Binhai Company failed to perform its contractual obligations, hindering the performance of the agreements, and that the facts found by the first instance judgment were erroneous. After the second instance upheld the original judgment, Tianyi Company applied to this Court for retrial solely on the ground that the second instance judgment erroneously applied the law. This Court instructed the Tianjin High People's Court to retry the case. During the retrial, Tianyi Company again argued that Binhai Company failed to perform its contractual obligation of cooperation. The Retrial Judgment upheld Tianyi Company's assertion, finding that Binhai Company failed to properly perform its obligation of cooperation, and on that basis made adjustments to the allocation of interests between the parties. After the Retrial Judgment was rendered, Tianyi Company again applied to this Court for retrial, claiming that the conditions for Wang Xifeng to obtain a mortgage loan were not fulfilled, Binhai Company's obligation to cooperate in obtaining the loan had not yet commenced, and it was impossible for Binhai Company to have failed to properly perform its obligation of cooperation.

This Court is of the opinion: Pursuant to the provisions of Article 13, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the principle of good faith shall be followed in civil litigation. During the course of litigation in this case, Tianyi Company repeatedly changed its position on the issues of whether Binhai Company performed its obligation of cooperation and whether it constituted a breach of contract. For the purpose of having this case again enter retrial proceedings, Tianyi Company denied the assertions it had persistently made during the first instance, second instance, and retrial proceedings, and denied the findings favorable to it in the Retrial Judgment. This conduct violates the principle of good faith. This Court will not support this ground for retrial asserted by Tianyi Company.

(2) Whether the ground for retrial asserted by Tianyi Company that the Retrial Judgment erroneously applied the law can be established

1. Whether the Retrial Judgment's finding that Binhai Company had the right to rescind the contract constitutes an erroneous application of the law

On March 8, 2004, Binhai Company and Tianyi Company signed the "Agreement on Transfer of the B Building of Binhai Commercial World" (hereinafter referred to as the Transfer Agreement), by which the subject property was transferred to Tianyi Company. On July 11, 2005, Binhai Company, Tianyi Company, and Wang Xifeng signed a "Supplemental Agreement", by which the three parties agreed that the purchase, loan, and property ownership transfer formalities would be carried out in the name of Wang Xifeng, and that Tianyi Company and Wang Xifeng would be responsible for obtaining the mortgage loan on their own and should pay the remaining purchase price of RMB 51,000,000 within 30 days after the signing of the agreement. However, Tianyi Company and Wang Xifeng failed to perform as agreed. On December 18, 2005, Wang Wei, the legal representative of Tianyi Company, sent a "Notification Letter" to Binhai Company, stating that Tianyi Company did not agree to convert the down payment of RMB 34,000,000 into a payment made by Wang Xifeng in her personal capacity, and was unable to obtain the loan within the agreed time limit, and proposed to rescind the contract. On June 28, 2006, Binhai Company filed an action to rescind the Transfer Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement. The first instance, second instance, and retrial judgments all supported this request. Tianyi Company applied for retrial, asserting that with reference to the provisions of Article 15, Paragraph 2 of the Judicial Interpretation on Commercial Housing Sales Contracts, Binhai Company failed to exercise its right of rescission within three months after the issuance of the Notification Letter by Tianyi Company, and its right of rescission had been extinguished before the lawsuit was filed.

This Court is of the opinion that this ground for retrial asserted by Tianyi Company cannot be established: First, Article 1 of the Judicial Interpretation on Commercial Housing Sales Contracts clearly provides: "The term 'commercial housing sales contract' as used in this Interpretation refers to a contract in which a real estate development enterprise sells to the public a house that has not yet been completed or has already been completed and transfers the ownership of the house to the buyer, and the buyer pays the price." Binhai Company is not a real estate development enterprise; it sold the house to specific parties, namely Tianyi Company and Wang Xifeng, rather than to the public. Therefore, the agreements involved in this case are not commercial housing sales contracts as referred to in that Judicial Interpretation, and this case is not subject to the above Judicial Interpretation. The time limit for exercising the right of rescission is a statutory prescriptive period; if the right is not exercised within the time limit, the right of rescission is extinguished. Therefore, the determination of this time limit has a significant impact on the rights and obligations of the parties. In the absence of explicit legal provisions, Tianyi Company's request to apply by reference the time limit for exercising the right of rescission provided in the above Judicial Interpretation for commercial housing sales contracts lacks factual and legal basis. Second, pursuant to Article 95 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, if the law has no provisions or the parties have no agreement on the time limit for exercising the right of rescission, and the right is not exercised within a reasonable time limit after a demand by the other party, the right shall be extinguished. For sales contracts for houses, the law has no provisions on the time limit for exercising the right of rescission, and the parties in this case did not agree on such a time limit in the contract. What constitutes a "reasonable time limit" shall be determined by the people's court in light of the specific facts of the case. In this case, after the Transfer Agreement was signed, Binhai Company had delivered the subject property to Tianyi Company for management and operation. Tianyi Company had paid a down payment of RMB 34,000,000 and had collected rental income of RMB 18,723,264.69 and security deposits of RMB 145,211 from tenants in the subject property from May 17, 2004 to June 26, 2006. If the contract were rescinded, it would involve not only the rights and obligations among Binhai Company, Tianyi Company, and Wang Xifeng, but also many issues such as the transfer of assets and tenants. Furthermore, the Notification Letter issued by Tianyi Company on December 18, 2005 merely stated that "we intend to negotiate with your company (Binhai Company) to rescind the above agreements." Therefore, Binhai Company needed sufficient time to consider whether to rescind the contract. Third, after issuing the Notification Letter and before Binhai Company filed the lawsuit, Tianyi Company neither performed its payment obligation under the Supplemental Agreement nor expressed any intention to continue performing the contract. Its breach of contract was ongoing. Considering the circumstances of this case, Binhai Company filed the lawsuit on June 28, 2006 after receiving the Notification Letter, which did not exceed a reasonable time limit.

2. Whether the Retrial Judgment's application of Article 94, Item (4) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China constitutes an erroneous application of the law

Tianyi Company argued that this case should apply Article 94, Item (3) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "if one party delays performance of its principal obligation and still fails to perform within a reasonable time limit after being demanded, the other party may rescind the contract."

This Court is of the opinion: The above provision applies only to situations where a party "delays performance of its principal obligation". In this case, Tianyi Company explicitly stated that it could not obtain a loan within the agreed time limit, could not pay the remaining purchase price of RMB 51,000,000, and proposed to negotiate the rescission of the contract. This constitutes a situation where the delay in performance of the debt frustrates the purpose of the contract, rather than merely "delaying performance of a principal obligation." Therefore, this case is not subject to that provision. The Retrial Judgment applied Article 94, Item (4) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "if one party delays performance of its obligations or commits other acts of breach that frustrate the purpose of the contract, the other party may rescind the contract." This application of the law is correct.

3. Whether the Retrial Judgment's application of Article 167 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China constitutes an erroneous application of the law

According to the Transfer Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement, the down payment of RMB 34,000,000 was to be paid in installments within 20 days after the signing of the Transfer Agreement, and the remaining balance of RMB 51,000,000 was to be paid within 30 days after the signing of the Supplemental Agreement. Therefore, the contract in this case bears the characteristics of a contract for installment sale, and the Retrial Judgment's application of the law is not erroneous.

4. Whether the Retrial Judgment is manifestly unfair

Pursuant to Article 5.3 of the Transfer Agreement, if Tianyi Company changes its mind and unilaterally proposes to rescind this agreement, or if this agreement is rescinded due to Tianyi Company's breach, Tianyi Company shall pay liquidated damages equal to three percent of the total transfer price and compensate Binhai Company for rental losses. Binhai Company shall return to Tianyi Company the remaining amount of the payments made by Tianyi Company after deducting the liquidated damages and compensation, without interest. The above agreement represents the true intent of the parties, is lawful and valid, and during the performance of the contract in this case, it was Tianyi Company that first proposed to rescind the agreement. The Retrial Judgment, taking into account factors such as the rise in real estate market prices and in order to balance the interests of the parties, ordered that Tianyi Company only needed to return half of the rental income it had received, i.e., RMB 9,361,632.35 out of RMB 18,723,264.69, and ordered Binhai Company to pay Tianyi Company interest of RMB 11,622,390 on the RMB 34,000,000. This is consistent with the principle of fairness. Tianyi Company's assertion that compensation for breach of contract should be limited to actual losses and its claim that it should also be entitled to a certain interest in the appreciation in value of the subject property lack factual and legal basis. This Court does not support them.

In conclusion, Tianyi Company's application for retrial does not satisfy the circumstances provided in Article 200, Items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law to Unconcluded Cases after the Implementation of the Amended Civil Procedure Law, and in accordance with Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial by Tianjin Tianyi Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Zhang Guorong

Acting Judge: Fu Shaojun
